pages.title: Accelerators
pages.note:
NVIDIA's fiscal 2028 guide of roughly 70% growth, delivered on 26 August and explicitly supply constrained, is now the anchor for every downstream estimate in this vault. Hyperscaler capital expenditure was framed at approximately $800bn in 2026 rising to $1.3tn in 2027, and NVIDIA's own forward commitments nearly tripled, most of it memory.

The theme's internal dispersion is the thing to watch. [[nvda]] and [[amd]] both held up through the week's selloff while the components they consume were sold hard, and [[avgo]] — whose disclosed AI revenue line ran $20bn of $64bn in FY2025 — sits between the two worlds. Scale and existing revenue were rewarded; capacity arriving in 2027 was not.

That split is the practical lesson of the week for this vault: within a single confirmed demand story, the market repriced by balance sheet rather than by exposure.

pages.title: Fabs & Foundries
pages.note:
The desk took its first position in this layer's anchor. [[tsm]] moved to accumulate on 10 August — not because anything improved at the foundry, but because everything downstream got expensive. First-half revenue up 35.6% with June alone up 67.9%, monthly disclosure that lets the demand curve be checked continuously, and a share price down about 7% on the month while the [[photonics]] names it supplies ran 48-77%.

The layer's own bottleneck is loosening: industry reporting has the CoWoS advanced-packaging gap narrowing from roughly 20% to 10% by end-2026 as capacity expands toward about 200,000 wafers a month by end-2027. That is why TSMC is being held as ballast rather than as a squeeze trade, and why the scarcity thesis on this map keeps migrating upstream toward lasers, substrates and glass. [[gfs]] and [[intc]] are unchanged on watch; neither had new evidence this week.

pages.title: Glass Substrates
pages.note:
Glass-core substrates for [[advanced-packaging]] — a natural extension of the packaging wave as chips grow larger and run hotter, and still the thinnest layer on this map.

On 17 Aug 2026 the desk moved [[lpk-de]] here from [[materials]], where it had been filed as an equipment name, and gave it its first verdict. That makes two names in the layer alongside Corning (GLW), which has surfaced only inside broader semis-selloff baskets. SKC Absolics and TSMC's CoPoS effort remain tracked as candidates rather than positions.

The layer's problem this week is timing rather than technology. [[aleabitoreddit]] reported Samsung Electro-Mechanics delaying its glass-substrate investment on customer reliability-evaluation bottlenecks, revising the start of operations to 2028, with SKC also pushing back — a delay in his own theme, which is the kind of disclosure worth weighting heavily precisely because it cuts against the poster's book. For an equipment supplier that pushes the revenue event out with it.

Glass stays a 2028-2029 layer on current evidence. Watch for the first disclosed tool order with a delivery year attached; that is what converts this page from a theme into a position.

pages.title: Hyperscalers
pages.note:
The hyperscalers are held here as the demand signal rather than as growth equities: if [[amzn]], [[googl]], [[meta]] and MSFT keep raising capex, the supply chain beneath them has a funded order book. Combined 2026 guidance moved to roughly $720-745bn from $695-725bn during late July 2026, with Amazon at $220bn and explicitly short of capacity even so.

The week of 3 August 2026 introduced a distinction the desk had been collapsing. Capex is not one signal — it matters whether it is funded. [[googl]] raised to $195-205bn against cloud revenue up 82%, and entered Core coverage. [[meta]] raised its floor $10bn and missed EPS badly, and was stepped to watch. Part of the increase across the group is memory cost inflation rather than incremental compute units, so the headline dollars overstate the unit demand reaching suppliers.

The second-order observation from the same week: the payers rallied while the suppliers fell. Owning both ends of the trade is no longer the same position.

pages.title: Materials & Packaging
pages.note:
Re-cut on 1 September after the desk read AXT's filing rather than the commentary about it.

[[axti]] is the theme's live position and it stepped down from accumulate to wait — not on weak numbers, which are the best in the book (revenue +164.8%, gross margin 8.0% to 44.9%), but on where the material is made. China is 66% of revenue, Tongmei manufactures there, and Chinese export permits for indium phosphide wafers are a named uncertainty. A [[chokepoint]] thesis is only as good as the ability to ship through it.

The theme's second mechanism showed up elsewhere this week: OSAT providers have warned that traditional packaging capacity could face a deficit exceeding 20% by 2027, with wire bonding the primary bottleneck and [[amkr]] a named beneficiary. That is the same cascading pattern already visible in legacy DRAM — AI server demand absorbs mature capacity, and early access becomes the scarce thing. LPKF ([[lpk-de]]) remains the glass-substrate expression and is unchanged.

pages.title: AI Memory
pages.note:
Still the highest-conviction supply theme in the vault, and as of 25 Aug 2026 the first one where the desk has taken money off rather than put it on. Both memory positions now sit at **wait**: [[sndk]] since 21 Aug on price, [[mu]] since 25 Aug on margin.

The reason is a single comparison. Micron printed an 84.6% gross margin last reported quarter; Sandisk's FY2026 GAAP gross margin was already 71.5%, against 16.1% two years earlier, and its investor day guides ~80% as a 2030 ambition. The industry is currently earning more than its own long-range plans, which is the definition of a peak rather than a plateau — unless this cycle is structurally different, and the desk has no evidence for that beyond its size.

The shortage itself is not in question. TrendForce has 3Q26 DRAM contract prices up 13-18% and NAND up 10-15% quarter on quarter, with capacity additions requiring roughly four years. [[amzn]] raised 2026 capex to ~$220bn explicitly on higher memory costs, which is the cleanest confirmation available: the hyperscalers' cost line is this theme's revenue line. That is also why memory and [[hyperscalers]] cannot both be cheap at the same time.

pages.title: Neoclouds
pages.note:
The theme returned to the verdict roster on 25 Aug 2026 through [[nbis]], initiated at **wait** — on roster because of attention and operating momentum, at wait because the desk has not researched it.

The structural case is the strongest it has been. Every hyperscaler in the book has now reported that it cannot meet its own demand: [[amzn]] guides capacity constraints into 2027 and raised capex to ~$220bn, [[googl]] raised 2026 capex to $195-205bn and printed a negative free-cash-flow quarter doing it. A neocloud with installed capacity sells into that gap at prices the hyperscalers themselves cannot offer.

The unresolved question is the one that always decides this theme: whether an operator buying depreciating accelerators and selling them forward on multi-year contracts is earning a spread or borrowing one. Contract duration against GPU useful life is the number that settles it, and it is the first thing the seats will be asked.

pages.title: Networking
pages.note:
The switching and custom-silicon layer that moves data between accelerators. [[aleabitoreddit]]'s [[mrvl]] thread stays sentiment-first — every drop reminds him of Jensen's 'next $1T company' comment — and this week he formalized a half-serious 'conspiracy theory' that [[nvda]] quietly supports the ASIC challengers (Marvell, MediaTek, AlChip) chipping at [[avgo]]'s custom-silicon share.

[[avgo]] is the incumbent custom-silicon giant; [[mrvl]] the challenger he watches most; [[nok]] a peripheral networking name. The layer overlaps the [[photonics]] story where switching meets optics ([[cpo]]).

pages.title: Photonics
pages.note:
The theme's third consecutive week of de-rating, and the first in which the desk's own research — not the analyst's — moved two stances.

The validation arrived from the best possible source. TSMC's VP of advanced packaging said foundries can scale the optical engine but the real bottlenecks to large-scale [[cpo]] deployment lie elsewhere, naming lasers, optical fibre, connectors and test. That is the customer of the entire [[siph]] stack confirming the scarce input is what [[lite]], [[cohr]] and [[sive]] make rather than what the foundry makes. TSMC separately sees silicon photonics taking over 50% of the optical transceiver market in 2027, and Soitec ([[soi-pa]]) reported more than ten capacity reservation agreements with $200m of photonics-SOI revenue described as a floor.

Against that, the desk moved [[mtsi]] to pass on MACOM's own later, softer laser guidance, and stepped [[axti]] down to wait on a China export-permit dependency no thesis had priced. [[sive]] held at wait after net sales fell 12% while its opportunity pipeline tripled, and [[aaoi]] held at wait with management having sold roughly $490m of stock at an average $103.51 against a $107.69 close. The theme's demand case has never been better evidenced; its financing and jurisdiction risks have never been more visible.

pages.title: Robotics
pages.note:
Physical AI is a high-conviction, high-euphoria theme, and August 2026 gave it its first hard public benchmark. Unitree listed in China and closed far above its IPO valuation, which [[aleabitoreddit]] reads as proof that public-market appetite for pure-play humanoids is much larger than assumed.

That benchmark reframes the page rather than settling it. Agility ([[ccxi]]) is the US pure-play, but it is still a pre-close SPAC with a confidentially submitted S-4, so the comparison prices a deal rather than a company — and the desk holds it at pass on exactly that distinction. [[tsla]] is the other humanoid name here and he explicitly rules it out as the exposure he means: Optimus sits inside a company far too large for it to move, and he does not think general-purpose capability is close. The component angle is thinner than the narrative suggests — he names Harmonic, LeaderDrive and Schaeffler as present almost everywhere, with Schaeffler claiming work with around 45 humanoid players, and smaller suppliers like [[vpg]] as niche possibilities.

The honest read is that the Chinese supply chain into Agibot and Unitree probably books revenue first, and that the investable Western exposure is still mostly structure rather than earnings.

pages.title: AAOI · Applied Optoelectronics
pages.note:
Applied Optoelectronics is the high-beta datacom optics position in the book — the name whose valuation case has always rested on a forward revenue rate rather than current earnings. The 800G ramp itself is real and company-confirmed: Q1 revenue was a record $151.1m, up 51%, with Q2 shipments guided at nearly four times Q1 levels.

On 3 August 2026 the desk stepped the stance from accumulate to watch. The $471m monthly rate anchoring the bull case — about $5.6bn annualised from H2 2027 — is roughly five times the run-rate management guides to, with Q2 at $180-198m and the full year around $1.1bn. It circulates in the [[photonics]] discussion as though it were the company's own estimate. Q2 is also guided to non-GAAP EPS between -$0.03 and +$0.03, so the 'one times forward revenue' cheapness describes a top line that currently earns nothing.

The trigger back to accumulate is management guiding toward the rate the thesis assumes, or a named CPO customer with committed volume — see [[amd]], where that read-through is still inference rather than schedule.

pages.title: AVGO · Broadcom
pages.note:
Coverage formally opened at **wait** on 1 September, and unusually the trigger is a negative catalyst.

For two years Broadcom has been the default beneficiary of every hyperscaler-diversifies-from-NVIDIA story. [[aleabitoreddit]] now reads [[nvda]]'s $3.5bn MediaTek investment as a deliberate move to build alternative ASIC leaders aligned to NVIDIA standards, with the explicit second-order effect of eroding Broadcom's position — and a likely counter-move pushing [[amd]], Broadcom and certain hyperscalers closer together. An alliance formed because a larger competitor is funding your rivals is a defensive formation, not an advance.

The desk has no view yet on whether the attack works: custom silicon is won on multi-year design cycles and a 2026 cheque does not dislodge a programme already in production. What changed is that the thesis now has an identified adversary rather than only a tailwind. The falsifier is specific — a flagship hyperscaler ASIC programme moving to [[mrvl]] or MediaTek.

pages.title: AXTI · AXT Inc
pages.note:
Stepped down from accumulate to **wait** on 1 September — not because the thesis failed, but because it succeeded and the desk then read the filing properly.

The indium phosphide price hikes [[aleabitoreddit]] has tracked since Q4 last year have landed: quarterly revenue up 164.8% to $47.6m, gross profit from $1.4m to $21.4m, gross margin from 8.0% to 44.9%. That is what a [[chokepoint]] looks like when pricing power arrives — revenue and margin moving together.

What changed is the jurisdiction. China is 66% of revenue, the substrates are made there by Tongmei, and AXT names the receipt and timing of Chinese export permits for indium phosphide wafers as a live uncertainty rather than boilerplate. Chinese private equity holders retain redemption rights over Tongmei, which is pursuing a Hong Kong listing. The company that solves the West's InP shortage ships out of the jurisdiction the shortage is about — and the export channel is the growth channel. A 17% fall on no company news, after 38.5% the week before, suggests the market is reaching the same place.

pages.title: CCXI · Agility Robotics
pages.note:
Agility ([[ccxi]], becoming AGLT) is the purest US mass-production humanoid play via the Amazon and Mercado Libre warehouse supply chains, and it re-entered the Core top fifteen in the 21 Aug 2026 review after Unitree's listing reset [[robotics]] sentiment across the board. The desk re-initiated it at pass.

The separation that matters here is between the company and the instrument. Digit is deployed with Schaeffler, GXO, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada and Mercado Libre, and [[aleabitoreddit]]'s operating read is sound — warehouse logistics does not require the acrobatic capability Unitree markets, so the comparison flatters Agility rather than embarrassing it. But $CCXI is Churchill Capital Corp XI, a pre-close SPAC. The combination was announced 24 June 2026 at roughly $2.5B with more than $620M of expected gross proceeds, and the Form S-4 was only confidentially submitted. Until it is filed publicly and goes effective there are no audited Agility financials and no way to know redemption levels — and those two unknowns are what determine what a share represents.

He holds a position sized in percent-of-float and argues the comparable upward, which is disclosed and honest of him, and is exactly the situation where a second opinion checks the structure rather than the story. The entry, if there is one, is post-close under AGLT on disclosed unit economics.

pages.title: COHR · Coherent Corp
pages.note:
Coherent is the vertically integrated one. Where [[aaoi]] and [[lite]] assemble modules around lasers they largely buy, Coherent grows its own indium phosphide — it doubled six-inch InP capacity ahead of plan and took datacenter and communications to 79% of Q4 revenue. In a [[photonics]] layer where the binding constraint is laser and substrate supply, keeping InP in-house is an allocation decision that makes merchant supply scarcer for everyone else on this page.

The desk upgraded it to accumulate in the 21 Aug 2026 review, and it is the desk's own call rather than [[aleabitoreddit]]'s — he referenced Coherent only as a back-reference that week, listing it among the names $NVDA invested in directly. The trigger was a disconnect: record fiscal Q4 revenue of $2.05B and FY26 revenue up 22.5% with EPS up 59%, and the shares de-rated anyway, alongside [[mtsi]] and [[sive]], while [[memory]] names ran. The market is repricing this group on gross margin rather than growth.

That margin gap is the whole bear case and it is real — Coherent guides roughly ten points below [[lite]]. The bet is that owning the [[chokepoint]] is worth more in a shortage than the module margin it gives up, and the falsifier is clean: datacenter gross margin has to actually expand, or vertical integration is just a lower-margin version of the peers.

pages.title: EWY · iShares MSCI South Korea ETF
GOOGL · Alphabet
pages.note:
Alphabet joined the verdict roster in the 16 Jul 2026 review on tier math alone — and the desk verdict says so: every mention in the corpus is contextual, never a mispricing argument. [[aleabitoreddit]] uses Google as the demand gauge of the AI buildout: the compute-constrained hyperscaler, the party that cut Meta off and taught the industry the cost of renting, and (this week) the counterfactual he believes pushed $AAPL toward AI-chip acquisitions. Watch stance; the upgrade trigger is a dedicated TPU-supply-chain thesis with named suppliers.

Rotated off the verdict roster in the 22 Jul 2026 review, one week after entering: the contextual mentions decayed and [[intc]] took the tier-math slot with the same context-name treatment. The demand-gauge framing survives the rotation — the desk still reads his Google mentions as evidence of structural compute hunger, just without a standing verdict attached.

pages.title: INTC · Intel Corporation
pages.note:
Intel entered the verdict roster in the 22 Jul 2026 review on tier math — crash-week mention volume, not a dedicated thesis. The desk's memo is blunt about the distinction: the corpus uses Intel as an instrument, not an idea. Its CEO's line that there is 'no relief in memory supply or pricing until at least 2028' is load-bearing evidence in the [[memory]] shortage case that anchors the [[mu]] and [[sndk]] positions, and 'INTC to LITE' is the span of [[aleabitoreddit]]'s market-bottom gauge for the whole semis complex.

The precedent is [[googl]], which entered the same way in the 16 Jul review and rotated off a week later when its contextual mentions decayed. Expect the same here unless a dedicated Intel thesis appears — foundry wins, advanced-packaging exposure, or CPO-adjacent capacity would make it analyzable inside this workflow. Until then the stance is watch, explicitly as a context name.

pages.title: LITE · Lumentum Holdings
pages.note:
Lumentum is the liquid, reported way to own the laser bottleneck that [[photonics]] is built on — the place where the theme shows up in guidance rather than in a model. It crossed 50% non-GAAP gross margin a full quarter ahead of its own timeline while shipping record 800G and starting 1.6T production, and that fact does double duty: it is the bull case for the stock, and it is the evidence that the laser shortage is a merchant-supply problem rather than an industry yield problem. The best operator is running ahead of schedule; it is everyone buying on the open market who is short.

The desk cut it from accumulate to wait in the 21 Aug 2026 review, and was explicit that this is a valuation call and not a business call. Nothing deteriorated — fiscal Q1 FY27 is guided above the quarter just delivered on both revenue and EPS. What changed is that after a year of compounding, the downside no longer requires the thesis to break; a single hyperscaler order-timing slip against a very high bar is enough. The desk rotated that capital toward [[cohr]], which holds the same [[chokepoint]] exposure without the finished-winner multiple.

The August entry stays open. This is a downgrade of future buying, not a sell.

pages.title: LPK.DE · LPKF Laser & Electronics
pages.note:
Re-categorised from [[materials]] into [[glass]] on 17 Aug 2026 and given its first desk verdict the same week — wait, no position. LPKF sells the LIDE laser systems that structure glass, the tooling a substrate maker buys before it can produce anything.

The timing of the initiation is unhelpful and worth recording honestly. The most recent thesis in the file is [[aleabitoreddit]] reporting a delay in his own theme: Samsung Electro-Mechanics pushing its glass-substrate investment out on a bottleneck in customer reliability evaluations, revising start of operations to 2028, with SKC also pushing back. For an equipment supplier a customer's slip moves the revenue event with it, and there is no partial credit — the tool order lands before the line runs.

Sixteen accumulated mentions is what put it in Core. That is attention gathered over months rather than conviction expressed this week, and being the second name in a near-empty layer flatters the rank further. The entry trigger is a disclosed LIDE order from a named customer with a delivery year attached.

pages.title: META · Meta Platforms
pages.note:
Meta sits in this book as the payer rather than the product — held to validate that the capex funding the [[photonics]] and [[memory]] supply chain is genuinely being spent. On that narrow question it delivered: 2026 guidance of $130-145bn, with the low end rising $10bn in a single quarter.

On 3 August 2026 the desk stepped the stance from accumulate to watch. Q2 EPS was $6.18 against roughly $7.14 expected, on $60.8bn of revenue and $31.1bn of quarterly capex, and the shares fell about 8%. The desk's own weekly recap carried the capex number and dropped the miss, which is the bias worth naming: a supply-chain lens reads hyperscaler capex as a demand signal and stops reading there.

The conclusion is not that the supplier thesis broke. It is that holding Meta and holding Meta's suppliers have become opposite expressions of one view — the equity is being derated for the spending that creates the read-through — and this desk already owns the supply side. Compare [[googl]], where the same spend is visibly funded by an accelerating cloud business.

pages.title: MRVL · Marvell Technology
pages.note:
Entered coverage at **wait** on 1 September, arriving fourth in the book in a single week.

The catalyst is NVIDIA's $3.5bn investment into MediaTek, which [[aleabitoreddit]] reads as [[nvda]] playing kingmaker across the ASIC ecosystem — creating the next leaders, then aligning them financially and strategically, the same playbook already run on neoclouds like [[nbis]]. Marvell is a beneficiary; the second-order effect is erosion of [[avgo]]'s incumbent position.

The Celestial AI acquisition is the specific asset. He estimates a $6-10bn standalone valuation against 2028 revenue projections of $500m and 2029 of $1bn, while noting honestly that Celestial books close to zero revenue today and loses about $12.5m a quarter. [[sive]] independently lists Marvell's Celestial as a potential optical I/O customer from 2028, which triangulates the horizon.

Everything here settles in 2028, and the stock fell 15.7% in the week the thesis improved — which is what happens to long-duration assets when the 30-year yield sits at its highest since 2007.

pages.title: MTSI · MACOM Technology Solutions
pages.note:
Moved to **pass** on 1 September, one week after the step down from accumulate, and the reason is that MACOM's own guidance moved against the position rather than [[aleabitoreddit]]'s read of it.

The desk held at wait with an explicit reversal condition: the H2 2027 capacity date pulling forward, or a first-generation CPO win appearing. On the fiscal Q3 call management described the continuous-wave laser as a 75mW part still in high-temperature operating life testing, with production a *potential* start in late calendar 2027 and near-packaged optics revenue from 2028. Capital spending stays near $60-65m a year, which is not what building merchant laser capacity costs — compare [[lite]] and [[cohr]]. Seventy-five milliwatts also sits below the ultra-high-power class Lumentum already ships into the same sockets.

The pre-review pass added a second exposure nobody had priced: China is now $133.8m of $342.2m of quarterly revenue, 39% and rising from 28%, inside a company whose largest segment is Industrial and Defense. The 17 August entry closed at a 16.6% loss and the 25 August add closed flat.

pages.title: MU · Micron Technology
pages.note:
Downgraded to **wait** on 25 Aug 2026, eight days after the desk opened it. The demand case did not break — 2027 DRAM and HBM remain sold out and allocation is running at 60-70% of requested volumes. What changed is that the desk measured the base.

Micron's quarterly gross margin ran 56.0%, then 74.4%, then **84.6%** across the three quarters to 28 May 2026, on revenue rising from $13.6B to $41.5B. That 84.6% is above the ~80% [[sndk]] presented as a *2030 target*. No [[memory]] cycle in the industry's history has held a peak near it, and at a $1.03tn market capitalisation the equity is priced as though it is a floor rather than a peak.

TrendForce has 3Q26 conventional DRAM contract prices up 13-18% quarter on quarter — steeply positive, and explicitly slower than 2Q26 on weaker consumer demand and a higher base. The shortage holds; the second derivative has rolled. The 17 Aug entry at $971.66 stays open and a trim was stamped 25 Aug. What reverses it: 4Q26 contract prices re-accelerating, or a quarter holding margin above 84% on bit volume rather than price.

pages.title: NBIS · Nebius Group
pages.note:
Back on the verdict roster 25 Aug 2026 at **wait**, having been dropped in week 33. It returns on sustained attention and on a Q2 that is hard to ignore: revenue of $582.3M, up 454% year on year and 46% sequentially, roughly 50% adjusted EBITDA margin in AI Cloud, $8.04B of cash, and reiterated 2026 guidance of $3.0-3.4B revenue with $7-9B exit ARR.

The rating reflects the desk's evidence, not the company. NBIS was dropped by the pre-review cap, so no primary research has been done on it and the stance rests on the analyst's posts plus the company's own release — a weaker footing than anything else on the roster. The open questions are specific: the depreciation schedule against GPU useful life, contract duration against that schedule, and how the buildout is financed.

The demand side is verified upstream rather than asserted, which is what makes the name interesting at all. [[googl]], [[amzn]] and [[meta]] have each reported capacity shortfalls at their own scale, and Amazon guides that constraints persist into 2027. A [[neoclouds]] operator with capacity already installed sells into a gap the hyperscalers cannot close themselves.

pages.title: NVDA · NVIDIA Corporation
pages.note:
The 26 August print changed this page's role in the book. NVIDIA guided fiscal 2028 revenue growth of roughly 70% against a 43.9% consensus and called the outlook supply constrained, while commitments rose from $119bn to $279bn on memory procurement — the number that validates [[memory]], [[mu]] and [[sndk]] from the buyer's side rather than the seller's. The desk moved from wait to accumulate the same week.

What makes that upgrade unusual is the context. Every layer beneath this one — [[photonics]], [[materials]], [[neoclouds]] — was sold hard in the same five sessions. The demand signal strengthened and the supply chain repriced anyway, which is the clearest evidence yet that the drawdown was about duration and positioning rather than about the AI thesis.

The unresolved item on this page remains the Portsmouth residual value guaranties: roughly 4.25GW, an aggregate obligation capped near $105bn, filed off balance sheet with an OpenAI affiliate as tenant. It is NVIDIA underwriting its largest customer's credit to get capacity built, and it is still absent from the analyst feed.

pages.title: POET · POET Technologies
pages.note:
Closed to pass on 28 August. The decisive evidence was not the desk's — it was [[aleabitoreddit]]'s own, three times in one month: cash-rich with huge capacity but no visible demand and a weaker moat; Marvell probably vertically integrating POET out of the interposer layer people had speculated about; and a place on his short list of names that overuse ATMs and dilution, alongside [[iren]].

He still holds a small position as optionality on the balance sheet and the Lumilens arrangement. The desk's judgement is that optionality is not a position when filed revenue rounds to zero across every year on record and the market has stopped paying for undated 2027 revenue.

The page stays because the [[photonics]] story runs through it — POET is one of the external light source paths [[sive]] supplies, so it remains a read-through even with no position. Reopening requires a named first-generation CPO design win with disclosed volumes.

pages.title: SIVE · Sivers Semiconductors
pages.note:
Sivers Semiconductors is [[aleabitoreddit]]'s single highest-conviction name and the highest-torque bet in the [[photonics]] sleeve — the InP laser supplier positioned at the chokepoint if co-packaged optics displaces pluggable modules. The structural argument is genuinely strong: Sivers and [[lite]] were the only two public laser suppliers named in the CPO programme that drew a $300m US award to [[gfs]].

On 3 August 2026 the desk stepped the stance from accumulate to watch. The reason is not the drawdown — it is that outside research put company numbers against the story for the first time and they point the other way. Q1 net sales were SEK 61.9m, down 22% year on year, and the $799m figure quoted as evidence is an opportunity pipeline rather than backlog. The [[poet]] wording change read as a material timeline upgrade resolves, in the only citable partnership language, to production readiness by end of 2026 — a milestone, not an order.

The falsifier is dated and close: the Q2 interim report on 27 August 2026. Existing tranches stand; new size waits for that print.

pages.title: SNDK · SanDisk
pages.note:
SanDisk entered desk coverage in the 16 Jul 2026 weekly review as the expression of the [[memory]] repricing, and its 2026 investor day is the most ambitious attempt anyone in NAND has made to engineer the cycle out of a cyclical business: FY2028-FY2030 non-GAAP gross margins of approximately 80%, operating margins of approximately 75%, adjusted free cash flow margin near 50%, and New Business Model agreements with eight customers covering roughly half of FY2027 bits and two-thirds of FY2028 bits on committed volumes with minimum financial guarantees.

The desk stepped it down to wait in the 21 Aug 2026 review, and the reason is worth recording precisely. The business case got stronger; the price got stronger faster, repricing roughly four years of that model in five sessions. One number circulating in [[aleabitoreddit]]'s summary — minimum contracted revenue reaching $93B — does not appear in SanDisk's own investor day release, which discloses no total committed-revenue figure. The desk could not source it and does not underwrite it.

The demand side stands on independent evidence: Phison's CEO expects 2027 capacity constraints more severe than 2026, since upstream suppliers need up to four years from plant construction to production. That is the same multi-year shortage logic running through [[mu]] and [[000660-ks]]. The test is contract renewal pricing, not demand commentary — committed volume only protects margin if the committed price holds.

pages.title: TSLA · Tesla Inc
pages.note:
Tesla sits in this book for one reason — Optimus as a humanoid programme pulling on the same [[robotics]] and AI-compute supply chain — and it is the clearest example the desk has of a scoring artefact.

In August 2026 it ranked thirteenth by priority score on 19 mentions, which put it inside verdict coverage. Reading the underlying posts dissolves that: nearly every mention is an incidental name-drop inside a multi-ticker recap, one carrying twelve symbols. The substantive references amount to an Optimus quote lifted from the earnings transcript and an unverified third-party claim about polysilicon equipment contracts that the analyst prefaces by saying he is not familiar with the supply chain. The score is measuring the analyst's posting format, not his conviction.

Recorded at pass on 12 August specifically so it stops presenting as a top-15 idea. It is worth keeping as a live reminder that mention-weighted attention scores reward list-posts, and that the [[aleabitoreddit]] feed contains a lot of them.

pages.title: TSM · Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co
pages.note:
[[tsm]] was upgraded to accumulate this week, and it is a deliberate disagreement with [[aleabitoreddit]], who treats the foundry as scenery — everything is built there, so it carries no edge. That was right while the small suppliers were cheap. After a week in which [[aaoi]] rose about 77%, [[cohr]] 71%, [[sive]] 50% and [[lite]] 48%, the supplier book is priced for the shortage while TSMC is down about 7% on the month with first-half revenue up 35.6% and June alone up 67.9%.

It is also the only name in the book whose demand curve can be checked every thirty days rather than every quarter, and it carries none of the qualification, dilution or single-customer risk that the small caps do. The offsetting caution is that advanced packaging is easing rather than tightening — industry reporting has the CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from roughly 20% to 10% by end-2026 — so the bottleneck this layer owns is migrating upstream into [[photonics]] and substrates. The position is ballast, sized like [[jbl]], not a bet on the squeeze.

pages.title: XFAB · X-FAB Silicon Foundries
pages.note:
X-FAB is a specialty foundry carrying two stacked theses: a value leg on cheap 2027 EV/EBITDA against the peer median with Melexis demand strengthening, and a free option on its 'photonixfab' silicon-photonics ([[siph]]) line that [[aleabitoreddit]] believes the market is not pricing at all. That [[siph]] leg is why it sits on the [[photonics]] page rather than with [[fabs]].

The desk retired it at pass in the 21 Aug 2026 review, and it is the clearest case yet of the gap this vault exists to record. He has argued X-FAB 29 times and every single one is bull, including a high-conviction add after earnings he said proved the bear posts wrong. Over the same twelve months, [[lite]], [[aaoi]] and [[axti]] all rose by multiples on the identical CPO and 800V thesis and X-FAB fell. A photonics-adjacent foundry that declines while the whole complex re-rates is not a mispricing waiting to correct.

The failure mode is specific: 'a rerating once the ramp arrives' has been the argument for a year and the ramp date has moved every time. A thesis whose payoff is permanently one catalyst away cannot be falsified, and cannot be sized. It also shows how [[conviction-tier]] can mislead — 29 bull arguments lift a priority score regardless of whether any of them proved out.

stats.definition: Assembling multiple dies (GPU + HBM) into one part — often the real bottleneck, not the fab.
A layer with so few capable suppliers that demand has nowhere else to go — where pricing power lives.
This desk's ranking: core = repeat, high-conviction mentions; watch = credible but thinner; radar = one-off name-drops.
Co-packaged optics — moving the optical connection onto the chip package itself; the next photonics wave.
High-bandwidth memory — stacked DRAM bonded next to the GPU; the scarcest ingredient in every accelerator.
A cloud built almost entirely of GPUs for rent, not a general-purpose hyperscaler.
Silicon photonics — making optical parts with chip fabs, so light replaces copper between GPUs.
